briefdescription.para: The complete command line, including argv[0], if any.

detaileddescription.para: A copy of the argv[] strings of main(), set when the options are parsed from the command line. When not empty, the reporters list it at the beginning of the report, and runner::add_top_suite() derives the default name of the top suite from arguments[0].

briefdescription.para: Whether the console output uses colours.

detaileddescription.para: Set by --color[=<when>], as in the GNU tools, where <when> is always, never, or auto, or one of their GNU synonyms (yes and force, no and none, tty and if-tty), and --color alone means always; the value is accepted only after =. The alternative --use-colour=<mode> or --use-colour <mode>, as in Catch2 and Boost UT, takes yes, no, or auto, and also accepts the other values of --color. Used only by the human reporter.

briefdescription.para: The patterns that select the suites and the test cases to run, one per nesting level.

detaileddescription.para: Each --filter=<pattern> or --filter <pattern> option adds one pattern; unlike the other options, --filter may be repeated. As with --grep in node-tap, the first pattern applies to the suite names, the second to the names of the test cases, and each further pattern to the names of the test cases nested one level deeper; the levels without a pattern are not filtered.

Within a pattern, | separates alternatives; a name matches when it matches any of them, as defined by utility::is_match(): * matches any sequence of characters, ? matches any single character, the match is case-sensitive, and the alternative must cover the whole name.

The suites and the test cases that do not match are reported as skipped, and their bodies are not called. The top suite is never skipped as a whole, since its body is main(), but when its name does not match the first pattern, all its test cases are skipped.
When the list is empty (the default), everything runs.

briefdescription.para: Whether the test cases are listed instead of run.

detaileddescription.para: Set by the --list-tests option, or by its short form --list. When set, the suite bodies run, as usual, to create their test cases, but the bodies of the test cases do not, so no check is evaluated. The selected test cases (see filter_patterns) are listed under the names of their suites, as Catch2 lists them:

The header is Matching test cases: when there are filter patterns, and the suites without selected test cases are not listed. The nested test cases are not listed, since they are created by the bodies of their parents, which do not run. The list is written to the console, unless the verbosity is silent, and to the output file, if any; no report is written, and run_suites() returns 0, or 2 after an option error.

briefdescription.para: Path of the optional output file.

detaileddescription.para: Set by --output-file=<path> or --output-file <path>. When it is empty (the default), no file is written. The reporter opens the file when it is created by initialise(); if the file cannot be opened, the error is reported on stderr, the report is written only to the console, and runner::run_suites() returns 2.

briefdescription.para: The reporter that displays the results.

detaileddescription.para: Set by --reporter=<name> or --reporter <name>, where the name is tap or human.

briefdescription.para: The level of detail of the console output.

detaileddescription.para: Set by --silent, --quiet, or --verbose; when several are given, the last one takes effect.

briefdescription.para: Whether errors were found while parsing the command line.

detaileddescription.para: Set by add_error(); returned by has_errors().

briefdescription.para: Whether the reporter name was not recognised.

detaileddescription.para: Set by the parsing constructor; returned by has_invalid_reporter().

briefdescription.para: Copy constructor.

detaileddescription.para: Copies all the members, including the strings and the results of the parsing, so the copy initialises a runner exactly as the original does; the copy is independent of the original.

briefdescription.para: Constructs the options by parsing the command line.

detaileddescription.para: Starts from the defaults, and parses the µTest++ options (--reporter, --silent, --quiet, --verbose, --output-file, --color, --use-colour, --filter, and --list-tests). The other arguments are ignored, since the applications may define their own, except for those starting with --, which are reported as unknown options.

A missing option argument, an unknown reporter name, an unknown colour mode, or an unknown option, is reported on stderr, the option is ignored, and has_errors() is set; run_suites() then returns
The errors are not written in the report, since the reporter does not exist yet.
The argv[] strings are copied, so they need not outlive the options.

argc
The argument count from main().
argv
The argument vector from main().
6.0.0
Scans the arguments after argv[0], in order, for:

listitem.para: --reporter=<name> or --reporter <name>, with tap (the default) or human;
--color[=<when>], as in the GNU tools, with always, never, or auto (the default), and their GNU synonyms (yes and force, no and none, tty and if-tty); --color alone means always;
--use-colour=<mode> or --use-colour <mode>, the Catch2 and Boost UT alternative to --color, with yes, no, or auto, or any of the --color values;
--list-tests, or its short form --list, as in Catch2 and Boost UT, to list the test cases instead of running them.

detaileddescription.para: When an option is repeated, the last one takes effect, except --filter, whose patterns are all kept, in order, one per nesting level; --color and --use-colour set the same option. An option argument given separately is the next argument, whatever its content; --color accepts its value only after =. The other arguments are ignored. The whole command line is copied into arguments, to be listed by the reporter; the option values are copied from there.

A missing option argument, an unknown reporter name, an unknown colour mode, or an unknown -- option, is recorded by add_error(), and the option is ignored (for an unknown reporter, has_invalid_reporter_ is also set, to stop the session in runner::initialise()); the parsing continues with the next argument.

briefdescription.para: Move constructor.

detaileddescription.para: Moves the strings and the vectors, and copies the other members; other is left valid, with unspecified strings.

briefdescription.para: Constructs the default options.

detaileddescription.para: The TAP reporter, the normal verbosity, no output file, automatic colours, no filter, and no command line; the test cases are run, not listed.

briefdescription.para: Destructor.

detaileddescription.para: Releases the owned strings.

briefdescription.para: Checks whether errors were found while parsing the command line.

detaileddescription.para: The errors were already written on stderr by the constructor; when set, runner::run_suites() returns 2. Never set for the default options.

true if at least one error was found.
6.0.0
Returns the has_errors_ member.

briefdescription.para: Checks whether the command line selected an unknown reporter.

detaileddescription.para: When set, runner::initialise() does not proceed: no output file is created, nothing is reported, no test is run, and run_suites() returns 2, even if selected_reporter was changed after the parsing.

true if the reporter name was not recognised.
6.0.0
Returns the has_invalid_reporter_ member.

briefdescription.para: Copy assignment operator.

detaileddescription.para: Replaces all the members with copies of those of other.

Not defaulted: it copies other with the copy constructor, and moves the copy into this instance, since the copy assignment of the vectors of strings uses std::copy, which triggers -Waggregate-return in the standard library headers of GCC on some targets. If the copy fails, this instance is not changed.

other
The instance to copy.
Reference to this instance.
6.0.0
Copies other with the copy constructor, and moves the copy into this instance; self-assignment is safe.

briefdescription.para: Move assignment operator.

detaileddescription.para: Moves the strings and the vectors, and copies the other members.

briefdescription.para: Records and reports a command-line error.

detaileddescription.para: Writes error: <text> on stderr, and sets has_errors_.

before
The start of the message, without the error: prefix.
value
The variable part, usually an option or a value.
after
The end of the message, without the newline.
Returns
Nothing.
The message is written only on stderr, since the reporter does not exist yet.

briefdescription.para: The configuration of a test session, and its command-line parser.

detaileddescription.para: The options are usually constructed from the command line, by runner::initialise (argc, argv), which creates the selected reporter and starts the session:
The applications that do not have a command line, such as the embedded ones without semihosting arguments, can define the options directly, starting from the defaults:
The applications can also parse the command line themselves, and adjust the result before passing it to the runner:

The configuration members are public, since any combination of their values is valid; only the results of the parsing (whether errors were found, and whether the reporter was unknown) are private, and are read by the runner.

The options own their strings (the command line, the path of the output file, and the filter patterns), so they do not depend on the lifetime of the caller's strings; the runner keeps its own copy of them.
